claim_boundary: deterministic larger-order holdout and stage-operation census, with no wall-time or full IC speedup claim
construction: only after a public hit, compute T=[b inverse mod q]U; center both coordinates; form B=y^2-x^3+x and E_B over Q; construct [b]P and [-a]P
falsifiers: an accepted public hit fails rational construction or reduction
a rational construction occurs before its public relation test
the independent audit disagrees on the query or relation census
public_test: for every admitted pair, test all 13 frozen integer vectors by actual finite-curve group arithmetic; record every test and every hit
query_filter: discard a pair if either Q-tG is identity or if the two public points coincide; record filtered queries
question: On a larger-order holdout, how often does the selected public vector family hit on a frozen query schedule, and do all detected public hits admit the same deterministic rank-one rational construction?
resource_cap: 512 scheduled queries per field and 13 vector tests per admitted query; no additional search after a public hit
schedule: for field p, query i in [0,512), and axis 0 or 1, take SHA256 UTF-8 seed:p:i:axis as a big-endian integer modulo subgroup order q; retain duplicate pairs
subgroup_generator: m times the reduction of (2,2), with m from the pinned coordinate-control result
target_fixture: Q=17G is built outside all experimental stage counts
verification: check rational nonsingularity, good reduction, rational relation, both point reductions, and same-target scalar replay; retain each failed event
